speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
text: asked the Minister for Home Affairs what are the criteria and process to prefer charges for capital offences.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The accused person will be held in remand while further investigations are conducted.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: After law enforcement agencies have completed their investigations, they will make their recommendations to the Attorney-General’s Chambers or AGC.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Where there are multiple accused persons allegedly involved in the same capital case, the same holding charge may be tendered against all of them initially.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: After investigations are completed, AGC will consider the sufficiency of the evidence gathered so far, and the specific role of each accused person.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The eventual position taken against each accused person would be based on the evidence available and their role in the case, and may therefore differ.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: I will illustrate this with the Downtown East incident in 2010.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: In the incident, the victim was attacked by a group of 12 Chinese persons in the aftermath of a settlement talk.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Five of the 12 accused persons had armed themselves with knives, a screwdriver and a bottle of chilli sauce prior to the settlement talk.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: During the talk, the accused persons accused the victim of staring at them.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Those armed used their weapons to stab and slash the victim, while others punched the victim.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The victim eventually passed away due to multiple incised wounds.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Holding charges of murder were initially preferred against the accused persons.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Members can see the different categories of involvement.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: I will illustrate with another incident which took place around Pandan Loop in 2014.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: There were four Indian accused persons, which I will refer to as “A”, “B”, “C” and “D”.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Prior to the attack, “A” told the three other accused persons that “A” and “B” would beat up the victim, “C” would act as a lookout and “D” would wait in the pick-up. “A” and “B” then took a metal rod each from the back of the pick-up and walked towards the Pandan Loop industrial estate.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The victim was subsequently found dead from head injuries due to direct blunt force trauma. “A” fled Singapore for India shortly after the incident.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Holding charges of murder were initially preferred against “B”, “C” and “D”.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Subsequently, there was careful consideration of the evidence and the respective roles played by them.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: It was noted that “A” was the main perpetrator and the three other accused persons knew that metal rods would be used before the incident, but there was no prior discussion to cause death to the victim.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The charges against the three accused persons were therefore amended to voluntarily causing grievous hurt with a dangerous weapon with common intention. “B” was eventually sentenced to three years nine months’ imprisonment and three strokes of the cane, while “C” and “D” were sentenced to three years six months’ imprisonment.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: As a lawyer, I fully appreciate and understand the sentencing precedents and principles.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Every case depends on its specific facts and extenuating circumstance, and not all of these facts may be readily available or obviously apparent to members of the public or the media.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: So, I have one supplementary question for the Minister of State, if I may.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: There has been some public discussion on the sentences handed out in the Orchard Towers case.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Can I ask the Minister of State's view on the sentences meted out and whether this is in accordance with the precedents and sentencing principles that have been clarified earlier?

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Indeed, we are aware of the public discussions on the Orchard Towers case.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: I think the common feedback that we received is that some of the sentences given look light, considering that someone has been killed.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: As I have explained earlier in my reply, for cases like that where it involves multiple offenders, the eventual charges and also the resultant sentences have to take into account of the culpability and the involvement of each of the accused persons.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: In the Orchard Towers case, there are seven accused persons.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Four have pleaded guilty to the respective charges.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Proceedings for the other three accused persons are on-going.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: The seven accused persons were drinking at Orchard Towers.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: When the group was leaving Orchard Towers, the deceased confronted them.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Four of the seven accused – Tan Sen Yang, Ang Da Yuan, Natalie Siow Yu Zhen and Joel Tan Yun Sheng – got into a fight with the deceased.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Tan Sen Yang was allegedly in possession of a knife and slashed the deceased a few times.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: The deceased eventually passed away from the knife injuries.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Tan Sen Yang has been charged for murder and the section 300(c) of the penal code.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: This offence carries the death penalty or life imprisonment with caning.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Ang Da Yuan, Natalie Siow and Joel Tan kicked and punched the deceased during the fight.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: They did not plan to assault the deceased and did not know Tan Sen Yang would use a weapon during the fight.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: As the attack by Ang Da Yuan, Natalie Siow and Joel Tan caused two minor and non-fatal abrasions on the deceased body, they were eventually charged with, and pleaded guilty to voluntary causing hurt with common intention.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: As Ang Da Yuan, Natalie Siow and Joel Tan knew that Tan Sen Yang was carrying a weapon, but continued to remain in his company, they were also charged with consorting with a person carrying an offensive weapon.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: This charge was taken into consideration in sentencing for Joel Tan.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: These sentences were consistent with the sentencing benchmarks set by the Courts.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: The remaining three accused persons, Tan Hong Sheng, Loo Boon Chong and Chan Jia Xing were not involved in the fight.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: That said, Tan Hong Sheng and Loo Boon Chong each face a pending charge of consorting with a person carrying an offensive weapon.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Loo Boon Chong also faces a pending charge of perverting the course of justice.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: He has been warned that no leniency would be accorded to him should he re-offend during this period, and he may still be charged for the offence.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: There were also some comments that the accused persons have received lenient sentences because of their race.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: These allegations are totally baseless and highly irresponsible.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: I assure the House that our criminal justice system does not give any preferential treatment based on race, religion, socio-economic status, educational achievements and so on.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: As I have explained, the sentences eventually given to an accused, depends on the evidence and his role.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: In the Downtown East example I gave earlier, the sentences given out to the 12 Chinese offenders ranged from three years and three strokes of the cane, to 12 years and 12 strokes of the cane.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: There were four Malay accused persons, which I will refer to as "A", "B", "C" and "D".

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: After an argument between "A" and the Indian victim's group in a club at St James Power Station, "A" felt aggrieved and contacted "B" who rallied "C" and "D" to arrive at the club, with the intention to attack the victim's group.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: When "B" stepped away for a phone call, "C" who was armed with a foldable knife, punched the victim and stabbed him repeatedly, while "A" and "D" punched and kicked the victim.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: The victim died from stab wounds to the thorax and head.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: When "B" returned to the club entrance later, the attack by "A", "C" and "D" had already been completed.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Holding charges of murder were initially preferred against the accused persons.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: After consideration of the evidence available and the roles played by the accused persons, the charges were amended.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: First, only "C" was charged with murder, as he brought along and used a weapon.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: He was sentenced to life imprisonment and 12 strokes of the cane.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Second, "D" was charged with voluntary causing grievous hurt with common intention.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: He was sentenced to eight years six months' imprisonment and eight strokes of the cane.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Another charge of voluntarily causing hurt with common intention was taken into consideration for sentencing.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Third, "A" was charged with voluntarily causing grievous hurt with common intention.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: He was sentenced to five years six months' imprisonment and six strokes of the cane.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: So, let me emphasise again: there is no preferential treatment based on race, religion, socio-economic status or educational achievements.
